newsitem.title: CONGO: Most Congo evacuation forces leave Brazzaville.
newsitem.headline: Most Congo evacuation forces leave Brazzaville.

text.p: Belgium withdrew the last of its evacuation force from Brazzaville on Saturday, leaving only the French of five forces stationed there to evacuate foreigners from the former Zaire if necessary.
Belgium, the United States, France, Britain and Portugal had assembled a total of more than 4,000 troops in Central Africa over the past two months.
They have been scaling down the mission since Laurent Kabila's rebels captured Kinshasa on May 17 without the much feared mayhem and renamed the country the Democratic Republic of Congo.
Belgium withdrew the last remaining men from its 700-strong force on Friday and Saturday, and Portugal, which had had the smallest of the contingents, pulled its troops out on Friday.
The last U.S. troops left the Congolese capital on Tuesday. "They were all on scheduled flights, either commercial or military," said a spokesman for the U.S. Embassy.

The U.S. Navy helicopter carrier Kearsarge, on which U.S. Marines were stationed off the Congolese coast at Pointe Noire, left on Saturday and then steamed north to Sierra Leone, where on Friday it evacuated 900 foreigners fleeing a coup.
The last British troops left Brazzaville and a rear base in the Gabonese capital Libreville early last week.
Captain Alexis Jaraud, spokesman for the French contingent, said he had no idea when the French troops, who still number about 350, would be likely to leave.
"We're staying on to reassure the French on the other side of the river," he said.
